problems.title: The plotted intervention population is smaller than stated
problems.source_location: Figure 5b/caption, current PDF p.8; Language/analysis/suppress_hall_scores.py, lines 84 and 183–210
claim: The caption assigns mean reduction \(0.19\) to a \(252\)-example top quartile of \(1006\) cases; final plotting applies another within-quartile median filter.
analysis: The first rule selects raw faithfulness below its full-data lower quartile; the second keeps its lower half. Distinct scores yield \(252\), then \(126\). Independently, current-PDF count-axis/vector geometry gives before counts \((11,36,79)\), after \[(11,4,2,8,5,7,5,11,16,57)\], each totaling \(126\). The code uses ordinary unweighted histograms. The mean lines therefore concern the narrower displayed subset rather than a verified full-quartile effect.
result: The plotted population disagrees with its caption. The excluded half’s effect is unknown; its inclusion could coincidentally preserve the rounded mean, but that is not verified.
repair: Recompute the full initial cohort or explicitly describe the second selection and smaller population. No corrected full-cohort mean is available.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The exact error changes one intervention estimate’s scope without showing suppression is ineffective.

problems.title: The maximum-activation statistic is length-scaled
claim: The paper defines \(\max_ta_{itj}\), but code uses \(\max_ta_{itj}/n_i\).
analysis: Non-BOS rows \((1,2),(3,4)\) have maxima \((3,4)\), versus released \((1.5,2)\). Repeating the rows preserves maxima but changes release output to \((0.75,1)\). A sample-dependent divisor cannot generally be removed by column scaling. This operator example does not assume actual repeated words preserve transformer activations.
result: PLS/VIP preprocessing differs and can encode length. Original activations/logs are needed for changed predictive results.
repair: Remove the divisor to implement the written maximum, or declare the length-scaled statistic and compare maxima/length-only controls on common splits.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The exact preprocessing mismatch has unmeasured downstream effects.

problems.title: The first cross-validation repeat is duplicated
problems.source_location: Language/train/hall_score_pls.py, repeat initialization/append and final plot aggregation
claim: Ten pooled out-of-fold repeat scores are stored as \((r_0,r_0,r_1,\ldots,r_9)\); the point is the first score and the error bar its duplicated-list population deviation.
analysis: For control scores \(r_s=s/10\), deviation becomes approximately \(0.30287875\), versus \(0.28722813\) with each once; first point \(0\) differs from repeat mean \(0.45\). These illustrate aggregation only. PLS fits training folds, so no fitting leakage is alleged. Repeat-level pooled variability is legitimate if identified.
result: Duplicate storage is a release error; point/error-bar conventions require clarification, with no corrected original uncertainty available.
repair: Store each repeat once, declare the point and deviation convention, preserve negative coefficients in records and label the repetition unit.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This local summary error does not eliminate the reported predictive signal.

problems.title: Categorical purity is not semantic cosine coherence
problems.source_location: Semantic interpretability definition; Vision/analysis/vit-noise-sae-interpretability.py, stats and PURITY_THRESH
claim: The paper describes top-\(16\) label cosine coherence with threshold \(0.75\). Active code uses maximum label fraction with threshold \(0.30\), leaving its cosine helper unused.
analysis: Eight labels each of orthogonal types give majority \(1/2\), passing code, but distinct-pair cosine \(7/15<0.75\). Conversely, \(16\) distinct labels with unit vectors \(e_r=\sqrt{0.9}u_0+\sqrt{0.1}u_r\) have pairwise cosine \(0.9\), passing semantic coherence, but majority \(1/16<0.30\). Including self-pairs preserves both decisions. These are metric-domain witnesses, not claimed pretrained embeddings.
result: The active metric is a different function; original labels/embeddings are required to reconcile interpretability percentages. Qualitative examples remain possible.
repair: Define normalized label embeddings and pair averaging, then apply the stated cosine criterion; alternatively identify the actual categorical statistic under its own definition.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The source/specification discrepancy affects a supporting analysis, with no replacement percentage established.

problems.title: Activation frequency divides batch means twice
claim: The code sums batch activation means and divides again by total token count.
analysis: One feature active on all \(4\) tokens yields \(1/4\) in one batch or \(1/2\) in two equal batches, while true frequency is \(1\). For equal batch size \(m\), released frequency is true frequency divided by \(m\); unequal sizes also misweight batches. At \(32\) images times \(49\) patches, the illustrative log shift is \(-\log_{10}1568\approx-3.19535\), potentially moving frequency bins.
result: The quantity depends on irrelevant partitioning and is not empirical activation probability. Actual selected features and percentages remain unrecomputed.
repair: Sum integer active counts and token totals, then divide once. Linearity proves partition invariance; regenerate actual bins to assess effects.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The counting error is exact but local to an analysis/sampling path; separate activation-count observations remain intact.
